question: Should varied feedback remain lifecycle-state based, or should the initial acknowledgment support configured choices or contextual selection?
rationale: Current code intentionally resolves one channel-compatible emoji before processing, while random and contextual alternatives change shipped configuration, latency, predictability, and per-channel behavior.

options.title: Keep lifecycle variety
options.body: Retain one deterministic initial ack and use queued, thinking, tool, done, and error reactions for varied feedback.

options.title: Add configured choices
options.body: Permit a backward-compatible emoji list with an explicit deterministic or random selection policy and channel fallback rules.

options.title: Add contextual selection
options.body: Design a pre-processing selector that can inspect inbound content, with explicit latency and failure behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep lifecycle variety
recommendation.body: Retain one deterministic initial ack and use queued, thinking, tool, done, and error reactions for varied feedback.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history spans both the current acknowledgment resolution contract and the lifecycle status-reaction alternative.
